cards.html: This track covers the probability and statistics an MSc in economics builds on: describing data, probability, random variables, the binomial and normal distributions, sampling, confidence intervals, hypothesis tests and simple regression. It assumes Math Foundations (fractions, percentages, powers, square roots). Sums and a few formulas are all the algebra you need.

Almost all modern economics is empirical: you test a theory against data. Econometrics, which every MSc requires, is statistics applied to economic data. Its central tool, regression, rests on everything in this track.

TopicWhere you will use it
Mean, variance, standard deviationSummarising income, prices, returns, risk
Probability and expected valueDecisions under uncertainty, insurance, game theory
Normal distributionSampling, finance, test statistics
Confidence intervals and tests"Is this effect real or noise?"
Correlation and regressionEstimating demand, returns to education, policy effects

SymbolMeaning
Σsum of (Σx means x₁ + x₂ + ... + xₙ)
x̄sample mean ("x bar")
μpopulation mean ("mu")
s, σsample and population standard deviation ("sigma")
P(A)probability of event A
P(A given B)probability of A when B is known to have happened
E(X), Var(X)expected value and variance of a random variable

Work the examples on paper with a calculator. Each skill ends with practice and answers. The tree splits after the first skill: the left path is descriptive statistics, the right is probability. They join at random variables, and the rest builds in a line towards regression.
